memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: For what mortal has ever heard the voice of the living God speaking out of fire, as we have, and survived? Go near and listen to all that the Lord our God says. Then tell us whatever the Lord our God tells you. We will listen and obey. - Deut 5:26-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The people make a request that reveals a deep need in the human heart: "You go near, Moses, and listen for us. Tell us what God says, and we will obey." They could not bear to stand before God directly, so they longed for someone to go between them and God — a mediator who could safely approach the holy One on their behalf and bring His words back to them.

This longing runs all through Scripture, because it reflects a real problem. Sinful people cannot stand in the unfiltered presence of a holy God. We need someone to bridge the gap. Moses served that role for Israel, faithfully carrying God's words to the people. But Moses himself was a sinner who would eventually die; he could point to the need but could not permanently meet it.

The whole story is pointing forward to Jesus, the perfect and final Mediator between God and humanity (1 Tim 2:5). Unlike Moses, He is both fully God and fully man, able to represent us to God and God to us flawlessly. He not only brings us God's words — He is the Word (John 1:1). And He does not merely relay messages; He brings us all the way to the Father. The longing for a mediator that trembled at Sinai finds its answer in Christ. In Him, you can truly draw near.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I recognise my own need for a mediator between me and a holy God?
- How is Jesus a greater mediator than Moses could ever be?
- Am I coming to God through Christ, my perfect representative?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I could never stand before You on my own. Thank You for Jesus, my perfect Mediator, who brings me all the way to You. I come today through Him, trusting His finished work. Amen.
